_comment: Octail's own egg. Octail downloads the official OpenRA release-20250330 AppImage of the chosen mod (Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn or Dune 2000) from GitHub, checks it against a SHA-256 recorded in the script (the project publishes none), unpacks the self-contained engine from its SquashFS image with unsquashfs (the AppImage is never run), keeps support/ (settings, logs, replays, custom maps) on a reinstall, passes the mod, name, port, password, public listing and the account requirement as OpenRA.Server arguments (values come from the environment, never pasted into the command), runs on octail-yolks' Debian image with .NET's invariant globalisation and adds the Ctrl+C stop, the log-only console (the server reads no input), the TCP port start check, install sandbox defaults and resource hints. The dedicated server needs none of the original game files.
name: OpenRA
author: eggs@octail.net
description: OpenRA is a free, open-source real-time strategy engine that recreates and modernises the classic Command & Conquer games: Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn and Dune 2000. One server hosts one mod.
startup: [ -x ./openra/OpenRA.Server ] || { echo "OpenRA is not installed: reinstall the server."; exit 1; }; [ -d "./openra/mods/{{OPENRA_MOD}}" ] || { echo "The {{OPENRA_MOD}} mod is not installed: reinstall the server after changing the mod."; exit 1; }; export DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=1; S="$(pwd)/support"; cd openra && exec ./OpenRA.Server Game.Mod={{OPENRA_MOD}} "Engine.SupportDir=$S" "Server.Name={{SERVER_NAME}}" Server.ListenPort={{SERVER_PORT}} Server.AdvertiseOnline=$([ "{{PUBLIC_LIST}}" = 1 ] && echo True || echo False) "Server.Password={{SERVER_PASSWORD}}" Server.RequireAuthentication=$([ "{{REQUIRE_AUTH}}" = 1 ] && echo True || echo False) Server.EnableSingleplayer=False

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# OpenRA installation script (Octail): the official release-20250330 AppImage of the chosen mod (Red Alert, Tiberian
# Dawn or Dune 2000) from GitHub, checked against the SHA-256 recorded here, and the engine unpacked from it with
# unsquashfs (the AppImage itself is never run). The dedicated server needs none of the original game files.
# Failures exit non-zero.
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
set -euo pipefail

## OpenRA release-20250330, the current release. GitHub and openra.net publish no checksums for the AppImages, so
## Octail recorded their SHA-256 (2026-10-23). A new release needs the tag and the three hashes updated here.
TAG=release-20250330
MOD="${OPENRA_MOD:-ra}"
case "$MOD" in
    ra)
        FILE=OpenRA-Red-Alert-x86_64.AppImage
        SHA256=3cb71c7428188c8526dd8916993fc16fa17ba5f28a35968a8267f3db9f2186fe
        ;;
    cnc)
        FILE=OpenRA-Tiberian-Dawn-x86_64.AppImage
        SHA256=b3d202d1bf701be5989c41c256d19bd2b1788694df01e343ade865cf1190706b
        ;;
    d2k)
        FILE=OpenRA-Dune-2000-x86_64.AppImage
        SHA256=7585986bf0cd488debaec3fadf853c1901003eff945dbad5de95b0b6bd781a67
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Installation failed: the mod must be ra (Red Alert), cnc (Tiberian Dawn) or d2k (Dune 2000), not ${MOD}."
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

apt-get update -qq
apt-get install -y -qq curl squashfs-tools python3 ca-certificates > /dev/null

if [ "$(uname -m)" != x86_64 ]; then
    echo "Installation failed: OpenRA publishes its Linux builds for x86_64 only (this node is $(uname -m))."
    exit 1
fi

cd /mnt/server
DL=/mnt/server/.openra-download.AppImage
URL="https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/releases/download/${TAG}/${FILE}"
echo "Downloading ${URL}"
if ! curl -fSL --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 1800 --retry 3 -o "$DL" "$URL"; then
    rm -f "$DL"
    echo "Installation failed: the download from GitHub failed."
    exit 1
fi
if ! echo "${SHA256}  ${DL}" | sha256sum -c --quiet -; then
    rm -f "$DL"
    echo "Installation failed: the download doesn't match OpenRA ${TAG}'s checksum for ${FILE}."
    exit 1
fi

## an AppImage is a small ELF runtime followed by a SquashFS image: the image starts where the ELF's section headers
## end, which the ELF header says
OFFSET=$(python3 -I -c 'import struct, sys
h = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read(64)
shoff, = struct.unpack_from("<Q", h, 0x28)
shentsize, shnum = struct.unpack_from("<HH", h, 0x3a)
print(shoff + shentsize * shnum)' "$DL")
rm -rf /mnt/server/.openra-unpack
if ! unsquashfs -q -n -o "$OFFSET" -d /mnt/server/.openra-unpack "$DL" usr/lib/openra > /dev/null; then
    rm -rf /mnt/server/.openra-unpack "$DL"
    echo "Installation failed: ${FILE} couldn't be unpacked."
    exit 1
fi
rm -f "$DL"
E=/mnt/server/.openra-unpack/usr/lib/openra
if [ ! -f "$E/OpenRA.Server" ] || [ ! -d "$E/mods/${MOD}" ]; then
    rm -rf /mnt/server/.openra-unpack
    echo "Installation failed: the dedicated server is missing from ${FILE}."
    exit 1
fi

## the engine is replaced; support/ (settings, logs, replays and your maps) stays
rm -rf openra
mv "$E" openra
rm -rf /mnt/server/.openra-unpack
chmod +x openra/OpenRA.Server
## custom maps go into support/maps/<mod>/<release>/ (the folder OpenRA reads user maps from)
mkdir -p "support/maps/${MOD}/${TAG}"
echo "${TAG} ${MOD}" > openra/.octail-installed

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed: OpenRA ${TAG} (${MOD})."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: Mod
variables.description: ra (Red Alert), cnc (Tiberian Dawn) or d2k (Dune 2000). Reinstall after changing it: the install downloads that mod.

variables.name: Server Name
variables.description: The name in the server browser (up to 64 characters).

variables.name: Server Password
variables.description: Optional: players must enter it to join. Empty = anyone can join.

variables.name: Public Server List
variables.description: 1 advertises the server on the OpenRA master server (it checks that the port is reachable); 0 keeps it off the list (players join by address).

variables.name: Require OpenRA Account
variables.description: 1 lets only players signed in to an openra.net forum account join; 0 lets anyone join.
